headword: {好奇心旺盛|こうきしんおうせい}

definitions.explanation: Describes a person who is eager to know about and try new things. Compound of {好奇心|こうきしん} (curiosity) and {旺盛|おうせい} (vigorous, abundant), and almost always a compliment.

examples.japanese: ⟦{弟|おとうと}→弟：00572_otouto⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{好奇心旺盛|こうきしんおうせい}だ。
examples.english: My little brother is full of curiosity.

examples.japanese: {好奇心旺盛|こうきしんおうせい}な{子|こ}ども⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{質問|しつもん}→質問：00888_shitsumon⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Curious children ask a lot of questions.

examples.japanese: ⟦{年|とし}→年：00486_toshi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}って→取る：00565_toru⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{好奇心旺盛|こうきしんおうせい}で⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{元気|げんき}→元気：00696_genki⟧で⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦{秘訣|ひけつ}→秘訣：13750_hiketsu⟧だそうだ。
examples.english: They say the secret to staying healthy is remaining curious even as you get older.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {好奇心旺盛|こうきしんおうせい}な⟦{性格|せいかく}→性格：03371_seikaku⟧: a curious nature
- {好奇心旺盛|こうきしんおうせい}で{行動的|こうどうてき}だ: curious and quick to act
- {子|こ}ども⟦のように→のように：30291_noyouni⟧{好奇心旺盛|こうきしんおうせい}だ: as curious as a child

USAGE:
Common in self-introductions, job applications, and profiles, where it presents a willingness to learn. In everyday speech it is often said with light affection about children and pets.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {物|もの}{好|ず}き: fond of unusual things — can carry a hint of oddness
- {野次馬根性|やじうまこんじょう}: rubbernecking curiosity — negative, about prying into other people's business
